questions.prompt: In the client–server model, which side initiates the connection?

options.text: Whichever has the lower IP address

questions.explanation: The client initiates by connecting to the server's known address and port; the server listens and responds.

questions.prompt: What does it mean that HTTP is stateless?

options.text: Each request is independent; the server keeps no memory between requests
No data is ever stored anywhere in the system
The client and server must be on the same machine

questions.explanation: Statelessness means each request stands alone; any continuity (sessions) is layered on with cookies, tokens, or a database.

questions.prompt: Which statements are true about client–server vs peer-to-peer? Select all that apply.

options.text: In P2P, each node acts as both client and server
A single program can be both client and server depending on the connection
Client–server has a central server that can be a single point of failure
In client–server, the server always initiates the connection

questions.explanation: P2P nodes play both roles, one program can too, and the central server is a bottleneck/SPOF. The client — not the server — initiates.

questions.prompt: A server claims a port and waits for connections; this is called binding and ____.
questions.explanation: A server binds to a port and listens, waiting to accept incoming client connections.

items.text: Server is listening on a known port
Client initiates a connection and sends a request

questions.explanation: The server listens, the client connects and requests, the server processes and responds, and the client uses the result.

questions.prompt: Match each role or term to its description.

pairs.right: Initiates the connection and sends requests
Listens on a port and responds
Every node is both client and server

questions.explanation: Clients initiate, servers listen/respond, stateless means no retained memory, and P2P blends both roles into every node.
